g_policy.reason: The offer copy states the 60-minute reward before play, and the user chooses whether to play. The decline and ad-failure fields leave the existing menu and reply access intact.

g_no_cash.reason: The reward is 60 minutes of in-app priority routing, not cash or something exchangeable outside the app.

g_no_chat_content.reason: The trigger event says the card only goes to users whose chats are mostly long roleplay stories. That targeting needs chat content rather than an app event alone.

g_no_free_removal.reason: The proposal removes nothing free; the decline field says replies retain their normal speed.

g_brand_safety.reason: The placement is a card in the s09 profile menu, a safe sheet away from characters and chats.

c1_revealed_value.reason: This existing-anchor reward gives priority routing, which the Janitor+ subscription sells according to s02.e06.

c2_evidence.reason: The 'what makes it work here' field says users skip a normal queue and get earlier placement in line. s02.e06 and m03 support priority routing, but neither establishes those specific queue mechanics as they work today.

c3_spares_payers.reason: The 'offered to' and 'subscribers' fields restrict the card to free users; subscribers who already have priority routing never see it.

c4_protects_subscription.reason: The reward expires after 60 minutes and is capped at two plays per day. Janitor+ already sells the priority advantage through s02.e06.

c5_moment.reason: The trigger places the card in the profile menu after the user returns from the Upgrade entry, rather than interrupting a chat task.

c6_fits_simula.reason: The flow uses a sponsored game following a detectable return to the profile menu. The ad-failure field says an unverified play does not turn on faster replies.

c7_specific.reason: The proposal uses the s09 Upgrade to Janitor Plus entry and the priority-routing benefit shown in s02.e06.
